name: split by a gcd with a random element raised to half the group order
mechanism: a product of equal-degree factors splits the residue ring into components; raise a random element to half the order of each component's multiplicative group, so it becomes plus or minus one in each component independently; the gcd of (result minus one) with the input collects exactly the components where it was plus one

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Cantor–Zassenhaus algorithm' in section Computational mathematics / Computer algebra: factor polynomials over finite fields

requires: a squarefree input already separated by factor degree
fails_when: each trial splits with probability about one half; needs a separate handling in characteristic two
